content:
What are Palomar's goals?

There's an explosion of interesting formally-verified math. The frontier includes proofs like Anthropic's Lean verification of Fermat's Last Theorem (https://www.anthropic.com/research/formalizing-fermats-last-theorem)

But these frontier proofs are heavy. The FLT one requires ~256GB RAM and 15+ hours to verify. Does Palomar want to support these kinds of proofs (eventually)? If so, there might have to be a "Pro tier" or some other form of paid submissions.

Zoomed out, is the idea that new math will be published to Palomar first, or that it will be published elsewhere with a palomar entry as supplement?
See #Palomar > simultaneous submission to arxiv @ 💬 and upvotes
